title: Varlock Releases Bumpy: A File-Based Versioning Alternative to Changesets
gist: Bumpy (@varlock/bumpy), an MIT-licensed monorepo versioning/changelog tool from the Varlock team, positions itself as a successor to changesets, claiming to address 120+ open issues with workspace/catalog protocol support, custom publish targets, configurable dependency propagation and git-free prerelease channels. Its edge narrowed after changesets v3 (August 2026); notable signals are that it was largely AI-coded and ships an LLM agent skill for generating bump files.

insights.claim: Bumpy, first unveiled in April 2026 by Theo Ephraim via Show HN, ships as @varlock/bumpy and claims to address more than 120 open issues from changesets.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Illustrates how backlog debt in incumbent open-source tools invites quick AI-assisted challengers.

insights.claim: Bumpy keeps the changesets workflow of reviewable markdown bump files in PRs but adds workspace: and catalog: protocol support across npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun, per-package custom publish commands, and a configurable three-phase dependency propagation algorithm.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Drop-in workflow compatibility plus broader package-manager support lowers switching costs for monorepo teams.

insights.claim: Bumpy's CI uses two commands in a standard GitHub Actions workflow with no GitHub App to install or separate action repo to trust, reducing supply-chain trust surface.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Fewer third-party integrations is a selling point amid supply-chain security concerns.
insights.quote: no GitHub App to install or separate action repo to trust

insights.claim: Version 1.14 added branch-based prerelease channels derived at publish time and never committed to git, targeting a pain point changesets' own docs call very complicated.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Prerelease handling is a concrete differentiator where the incumbent concedes weakness.

insights.claim: The Show HN thread acknowledged Bumpy was coded using AI, yet it is already used to release Varlock and 25+ related libraries and plugins.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Evidence that AI-built developer tools are reaching production use, compressing the time and cost to challenge incumbents.
insights.quote: was coded using AI, but carefully
insights.locator: A Show HN thread was candid

insights.claim: Bumpy ships an agent skill that teaches LLMs to inspect git changes, identify affected packages and generate bump files, installable via the Vercel Labs skills CLI, GitHub CLI or as a Claude Code plugin.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Developer tools are starting to ship agent-facing interfaces, signaling agent skills as a new distribution channel.

insights.claim: The changesets v3 release in August 2026 closed many of the long-standing issues Bumpy originally targeted, and Bumpy's own docs credit it as a substantial cleanup.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Challenger advantages can evaporate quickly when incumbents respond; narrows Bumpy's moat.
insights.locator: Competition tightened with the changesets v3

insights.claim: Bumpy still claims remaining gaps in changesets v3 around configurable propagation, catalogs, custom publish targets and prerelease workflows, and adds a bumpy generate command to create bump files from commits, bridging to semantic-release style.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Positions Bumpy as a hybrid that could pull users from both file-based and commit-based release tools.
insights.locator: Competition tightened with the changesets v3

insights.claim: Teams evaluating migration have opened issues flagging gaps such as Yarn 4.10 catalog detection.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Early maturity gaps remain a migration risk.
insights.locator: A Show HN thread was candid
